column1: # The most memory each test may use, in MiB (docs/engineering-guide.md,
#   go       a Go test package, by directory: the test binary's peak, under
#            `go test -exec ci/run_capped.py` (the compile is the go command's,
#   go-race  the same package's binary built with -race (the weekly run)
#   meson    a datapath meson test (datapath/meson.build passes it as
#            UPF_TEST_MEM_MB; ci/run_capped.py is the default test setup's
#   lane     a ci/ lane's bessd (ci/bess-env.sh: bessd_launcher,
# ci/run_capped.py and ci/bess-env.sh run each in a cgroup at 1.5x its row (at
# least 32 MiB above) and fail it when its peak is above the row;
# ci/check-test-memory.py fails when a test has no row, when a row is above the
# 1024 MiB ceiling without a "# above the ceiling: <reason>" line just above
# it, or when `go test -p 2` could hold more than 2048 MiB at once.
# Calibration: the larger of the two peaks the wrapper can report -- the
# scope's memory.peak and, with no user manager, wait4's ru_maxrss (a lane's
# daemon: its VmHWM) -- times 1.25, rounded up to 8 MiB. The two differ: a
# test binary's own pages count in ru_maxrss, but the kernel charges a page to
# the cgroup that first read it (cgroup-v2.rst, "Memory Ownership": the go
# command's, which linked the binary), so a small package's memory.peak is a
# Measured 2026-11-04 on this tree (base b03aa8f), Go 1.27.2, GOMAXPROCS=2,
# BESS pin 941feb51, each run alone in its own capped scope with
# UPF_TEST_MEM_MEASURE=1 (UPF_TEST_MEM_NO_SCOPE=1 for the second peak); the
# commands are in docs/engineering-guide.md, "Test memory". After each row:
# above the ceiling: it holds 2.1M counted rules (~1.3 GB live heap, gctrace),
# the compiler's own session model, because one reply of every rule passes the
# daemon's 64 MiB message bound (internal/scaletest/scaletest.go:101) only at
# about 2M: with fewer, no whole-module read is refused and the test proves
# nothing about the chunked read (UG-B1; design.md cites the test at that
# scale). ci/go-test.sh runs it by itself and skips it in the package's run.
# A lane's row bounds its bessd (--mem_backing=normal), with the lanes' packet
# pool of 32768 buffers (ci/bess-env.sh, BESSD_POOL). bessd alone with no graph
# peaks at 707 MiB with the default pool (--buffers=262144, bess
# above the ceiling: the graph's PacketStore refuses a pool smaller than twice
# its max_packets (65536) plus its 4096-slot ingress ring (BESS 941feb51
# core/modules/packet_store.cc:209-219), and bessd takes only a power of two
# (core/runtime/opts.cc:248-258): the lane runs 262144 buffers, the default.
